newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah ignores East Timor protests.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah ignores East Timor protests.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was little moved in sudbued dealings on Thursday as players largely shrugged off demonstrations in East Timor.
Jakarta dealers said it was not clear whether operators were waiting for further developments in East Timor or just had no interest in trading due to a lack of fresh leads.

Thousands of Timorese prepared to march from the University of East Timor on Thursday in support of Nobel peace laureate Bishop Carlos Belo as protests in Dili entered their third day. The protests have been sparked by Indonesian criticism of Belo for saying in an interview with a German magazine that East Timorese were being treated like dogs.
One local bank dealer said many players were seen reducing speculative exposures as the year-end approached because they had met overall targets for the year.
"There are only a few weeks to go and people do not want to take any more risks. They just square off," the dealer said.

Spot rupiah was at 2,335.80/36.00 at 0425 GMT against an opening of 2,336.0/36.5. Continued ample money market liquidity and the possibility of a higher central bank fixing provided some support to the dollar, dealers said.

They said there was no consensus on whether the central bank would raise its intervention rate again on Thursday after raising it by one point to 2,335/2,527 and the conversion rate to 2,335/2,383 on Wednesday, for the second time this week.
In Malaysia, the ringgit came under pressure from local corporate and offshore fund demand for dollars.

"Local players were collecting dollars around 2.5240 this morning and after the break of 2.5250, we're looking for 2.5270/80. I think the year-end dollar demand is in play again," said a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore.
Some dealers said the market had begun to build fresh positions against the ringgit expecting a renewed decline in the Malaysian unit.
"Some investment house in Hong Kong is buying (dollars). There is also some demand from Sydney side," another U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said.
He said dollar/ringgit was well bid, but some selling could be expected at the 2.5265 level.
The ringgit was quoted at 2.5260/65 to the dollar at 0425 GMT against 2.5245/55 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday.
Further south, the Singapore dollar saw scant interest and dealers said its downside was likely to be contained by large U.S. dollar sell orders above S$1.4020.
One dealer said there was talk of between $100-200 million worth of orders, but he added that the U.S. dollar was likely to stay supported around S$1.4000.
The Thai baht was also little moved as players focused increasingly on Sunday's general election.
A Bangkok dealer said the market was adopting a wait-and-see attitude. "People either chose to square positions or avoided taking big positions before the result is known on Monday," he said.
Meanwhile, the Thai overnight interbank rate slipped on reduced demand for funds as most finance companies had fulfilled their cash reserve requirement.
Dealers said the lower cost of imported short-term swap funds on Wednesday also helped market sentiment with some finance firms staying on the offer side on Thursday morning.
"I think interbank rates would stay put with a slightly lower bias on the eve of the Thai election," a dealer at a foreign bank said.
